This page walks through what the editor can do. Each section is a short list of things to try, so tick them off as you go. Everything you change is saved in this browser.
Write
Click anywhere and type. Enter in the title moves into the page.
Type `/` on a line to pick a block: text, a heading, a list, a checklist, a quote, a divider or a table.
Start a line with `#`, `-`, `[]`, `>` or `---` and a space to make that block as you type.
Select some text to make it **bold**, *italic*, <u>underlined</u>, ~~struck through~~ or `code`.
Hover a block and drag the grip on its left to move it. Click the grip for a menu: Turn into changes the kind of block, and Copy link copies an address that opens the page at that block.
Use the pill at the top to insert text, a checklist or a table without the keyboard.
Tables

Click a cell to type in it, and press Tab to move to the next one. Hover the table for a handle on each row and each column. Its menu inserts, moves and deletes. From the keyboard, Alt+Shift+R opens the row menu and Alt+Shift+C the column menu.
Pages
Open the page menu at the top left to switch pages, add a page or a subpage, rename, duplicate, delete, or download the page as Markdown.
Type `@` to link to another page, like [[page:to-do-list|To-do list]]. Click the link to open that page.
Click the icon above the title to pick an emoji or an icon for the page. The Icons tab also sets its color. Remove takes it away. A page without one shows Add icon when you point at its title.
On a wide window, hover the short lines at the left edge to see the outline of this page, and click a heading to jump to it.
A new page starts empty and offers templates. This page is the first of them.
Comments
Select a passage and choose Comment to start a thread beside it.
Reply in the thread, react to a comment with an emoji, and resolve the thread when it is dealt with.
Write @Assistant in a comment to ask the assistant to shorten, reword or clarify the passage.
Hide and show every comment with the button at the top right.
The assistant
The assistant lives in the bar at the bottom of the page. It edits the page itself, and a small flag with its name shows where it is writing.
Ask it for a change, such as: Add three tasks under the first heading.
Select some text and choose Ask AI to ask about that passage.
Ask it to leave comments on the page. Its comments carry its icon.
After an edit, pick one of the follow-ups it suggests.
Attach a file or an image with the paperclip. Where the browser can turn speech into text, dictate with the microphone.
Open History to go back to an earlier chat of this visit, start a new one or delete one.
Drag the grip to move the bar, and drag its edges or corners to resize it. Both also work from the keyboard.
Minimise it to a round button. A blue dot on the button means there is something you have not seen.
Review an edit
The menu in the composer sets how edits land. In Manual, each edit is highlighted in blue and waits for you. In Auto, edits land straight away.
Accept keeps the edit. So does Cmd+Enter, or Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Linux.
Undo puts the page back as it was. So does Cmd+Backspace, or Ctrl+Backspace, while the caret is outside the page.
Ask for change takes you back to the assistant with that edit attached.
Editing the page yourself also keeps the edit, so Undo never takes your own changes with it.
This preview answers from a script, with no model behind it, so the assistant knows a handful of requests. Its suggestions are the ones it can do.
